findings: The one LilScript compiler (24968659) rebuilt the port from the unified/trough/VFile rewrite; dist/unified.esm.js, dist/unified.node.js, dist/unified.closed.js, dist/vfile.esm.js and dist/vfile.node.js are compiler output plus the license banner (and, in the Node files, the node:path, node:process and node:url imports vfile makes under `node`), with no post-minifier.
dist/unified.cjs, dist/unified.umd.js and dist/vfile.cjs are esbuild format conversions of the compiler's ESM (not minified): post-processed by esbuild, not compiler-written (plan M12.2).

vfile's #minpath, #minproc and #minurl now resolve per export condition as upstream's do (node:path, node:process and node:url under `node`, the shims elsewhere); the default program's working directory is the shim's '/', so dist/unified.esm.js went from 4199 to 4157 Brotli-11.
Against the source-built official graph: Terser 4339, Oxc 4411, esbuild 4612 Brotli-11; ours 4157.
This compiler renames no properties, so the closed lane (lilscript.closed.toml) differs from the npm compile only through its optimizer settings: 4164 vs 4157 Brotli-11.
Upstream version gap: pinned 11.0.5; no compatibility upgrade is implied.
